findings.title: Classify compact JSON independently of its byte encoding
findings.description: The byte prefilter returns None before parsing valid UTF-16 or UTF-32 JSON because reserved keys contain interleaved NULs. In two isolated committed fixtures, a compact envelope encoded as UTF-16/UTF-32 .json with its gzip payload deleted is accepted by evidence_exists and produces audit errors=[]. It also accepts deliberately mismatched expected tested commit, command and zero exit code although the envelope records exit 1. json.loads recognizes both as gzip-v1, but read returns their metadata bytes as plain evidence. The prior filename bypass is closed for UTF-8 content, yet the same missing-payload/integrity/metadata bypass remains through standard JSON encodings.
findings.requested_change: Classify every supported JSON encoding before returning plain evidence, or detect and reject reserved storage-shaped content in unsupported encodings. Apply malformed/truncated and escaped-marker protections consistently to UTF-16/32 while preserving opaque historical bytes. Add bounded negative tests covering UTF-16/32 with and without BOM, missing/tampered payloads and mismatched tested/command/exit bindings, including audit and generic availability paths.
